questions.question: What is a controller in Rails MVC?
questions.title: Controllers in Rails MVC
questions.direct_answer: In Rails MVC, the controller is the orchestrator: it takes a routed request, pulls data from models, and hands it to the view. It's a class (PostsController < ApplicationController) with one method per action (index, show, create). Each action sets instance variables for the view (@posts = Post.all) and renders (render :index by convention, or render json:). Controllers hold no business logic — they find, authorize, call a service, and render. The model owns data and rules; the view owns presentation; the controller wires them. Keep controllers thin and readable: a glance at an action should show the flow (find -> authorize -> render).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the controller is the orchestrator (takes a routed request, pulls from models, hands to the view) and holds no business logic.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Stuffing business logic into controllers (should live in models/services), or reading instance vars that the view can't see (controller @vars ARE the view's data).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: In Rails MVC the controller is the orchestrator: it takes a routed request, pulls data from models (@vars), and renders. No business logic — find, authorize, render. Keep it thin.

sections.content:
routed request -> controller -> models (@vars) -> view. No business logic; find, authorize, render.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[routed request] --> C[controller action]
  C --> M[models: @posts = Post.all]
  C --> A[authorize / call service]
  M --> V[view via @vars; render]
```

sections.title: A controller in MVC
sections.content:
```ruby
class PostsController < ApplicationController
  # GET /posts -> index
  def index
    @posts = Post.all             # pull from the model -> @var for the view
    # render app/views/posts/index.html.erb by convention
  end

  # GET /posts/:id -> show
  def show
    @post = Post.find(params[:id])   # find one
    authorize @post                  # authorize (Pundit/etc.)
    # render :show by convention
  end

  # POST /posts -> create
  def create
    @post = Post.new(post_params)
    if @post.save
      redirect_to @post
    else
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  end

  private
  def post_params; params.require(:post).permit(:title, :body); end
end
# Thin: find, authorize, render. Logic lives in the model or a service.
```
